scope: How a feature-gated application schema is registered in the native schema registry.
question: Lane C needs to add dimabot/src/schemas/channel_ai_personality.schema.rs (feature channel-ai-personality). Does it belong in src/schemas/mod.rs::definitions(), which currently returns an unconditional [&'static SchemaDefinition; 42]?
resolution: No. definitions() stays at 42 entries and is NOT modified by this team.
rationale: The repo precedent is that feature-gated schema modules are declared with #[cfg(feature = ...)] and are deliberately absent from definitions(). Verified in the accepted base: channel_fish_voice_favorites (channel-fish-voice-favorites), channel_moderation_settings (channel-moderation-settings), channel_tts_settings (channel-tts-settings), follow_defense_* (follow-defense-schemas), moderation_action_log (moderation-action-log-schema), moderation_decision (moderation-decision-schema), moderation_variation (moderation-variation-storage), and the media_extension_schemas group are all declared behind a feature gate and appear nowhere in the 42-entry array. There is no separate registration function for gated schemas; they are reachable only through their module path.

centralPatch.change: Add the gated declaration only. Do NOT change the definitions() array length or append an entry.

note: The #[path] attribute is required because the file carries the .schema.rs suffix, exactly like the existing channel_tts_settings and channel_moderation_settings declarations.

verification.note: Authoring wave only. No Cargo, rustfmt, Node, Docker or network command has been run.
